nodes.statement: f(y) >= f(x)+<grad f(x),y-x> for every y in R^d.
x* minimizes f over V iff <grad f(x*),y-x*> >= 0 for every y in V.
hypotheses: f convex and differentiable on an open set containing V
finite-dimensional Euclidean setting inherited from chapter

nodes.statement: First-order inequality plus Theorem 2.7 gives f(y)>=f(x*) on V.
If <grad f(x*),y-x*><0, z(alpha)=alpha*y+(1-alpha)*x* lies in V for alpha in [0,1]; h(alpha)=f(z(alpha)) has h'(0)<0. Small positive alpha decreases f, contradicting minimization.

nodes.region: Theorem 2.13 statement and printed14 proof continuation
nodes.statement: Ordinary OGD uses g_t=grad ell_t(x_t), predicts x_t before ell_t, and has R_T(u)<=D^2/(2eta_T)+sum_{t=1}^T eta_t*||g_t||_2^2/2-||x_{T+1}-u||_2^2/(2eta_T). Constant eta gives R_T(u)<=||u-x_1||_2^2/(2eta)+(eta/2)*sum_{t=1}^T||g_t||_2^2-||x_{T+1}-u||_2^2/(2eta).
hypotheses: V nonempty closed convex subset R^d; D=sup_{x,y in V}||x-y||_2
losses convex differentiable on open set containing V
nodes.proof_continuation: Before bounding by D^2, printed14 keeps ||x_1-u||^2/(2eta_1)-||x_{T+1}-u||^2/(2eta_T)+sum_{t=1}^{T-1}(1/eta_{t+1}-1/eta_t)*||x_{t+1}-u||^2/2+sum_{t=1}^T eta_t*||g_t||^2/2. Constant-rate telescope keeps the two endpoint squared distances and the positive gradient-square sum.
nodes.scope_note: Context only: this extraction does not claim full proof reconstruction of Theorem2.13 or Lemma2.12.

nodes.statement: The ||g_t||_2^2 terms arise because x_t is output before observing ell_t; these terms become non-positive when ell_t is observed before x_t. Forward reference: Section 15.5.1.
nodes.interpretation: Structural statement about the prescient update and correction terms, not a claim that every prescient regret total is non-positive or that the ordinary OGD update may merely flip a sign.

nodes.statement: Closed means every real sublevel set is closed; proper means nowhere -infinity and finite somewhere.
For proper f:R^d -> (-infinity,+infinity], g in partial f(x) means f(y)>=f(x)+<g,y-x> for all y in R^d. Subdifferentiable at x means partial f(x) nonempty.

For real-valued f:R^d->R and convex V, nonempty partial f(x) for every x in V implies restriction f|V is convex. Proof uses a subgradient at y=lambda*x1+(1-lambda)*x2, then weighted addition of two support inequalities.
hypotheses: f globally real-valued in printed theorem
nodes.domain_caution: Algorithm losses may be +infinity outside V. The displayed proof only needs finite values at points in V, but that adaptation must be recorded as a derived bridge, not as literal statement identity.

nodes.statement: Strict convexity: f(alpha*x+(1-alpha)*y)<alpha*f(x)+(1-alpha)*f(y) for distinct x,y in convex domain and 0<alpha<1.
B_psi(x;y)=psi(x)-psi(y)-<grad psi(y),x-y>; B_psi:X x int X -> R.
hypotheses: psi differentiable on nonempty int X
X is domain of psi; ambient R^d

nodes.region: Opening paragraph after distance-generating function terminology
nodes.statement: For y in int X and x in X, psi(x)>=psi(y)+<grad psi(y),x-y>, with equality only x=y; hence B_psi(x;y)>=0.
hypotheses: strict convexity of psi and differentiability at y
nodes.note: Opening sentence mentions x,y interior, then the stronger displayed prose explicitly permits x in X; competitor u need not be interior.

nodes.statement: B_psi(z;x)+B_psi(x;y)-B_psi(z;y)=<grad psi(y)-grad psi(x),z-x>.
hypotheses: B_psi is Bregman divergence for psi:X->R
nodes.proof_status: Identity stated without displayed proof on this page; follows algebraically from Definition 6.4, which is recorded as an algebraic dependency, not a quoted proof.

nodes.statement: For t=1,...,T: receive ell_t, choose x_t in argmin_{x in V}(ell_t(x)+B_psi(x;x_{t-1})/eta_t), then pay ell_t(x_t).
hypotheses: V nonempty closed convex; printed V subset X subseteq R^d
psi:X->R strictly convex and differentiable on int X
x_0 in int X (membership x_0 in V is not required in the printed box)
nodes.existence: Selection of argmin is part of the algorithm trajectory. These printed conditions alone are not an existence proof; theorem is conditional on a selected trajectory.
nodes.domain: ell_t finite on V. For t>=1, selected x_t lies in V. Each Bregman reference x_{t-1} must lie in int X.

nodes.statement: Observing the current loss changes the oracle from gradient-only access to function access. Best response gives non-positive regret, but optimistic arguments need specific negative terms supplied by Prescient OMD.
nodes.scope_note: No quantitative theorem extracted from motivational comparisons.

nodes.statement: Theorem hypotheses together with Algorithm 15.8 requirements.
hypotheses: psi:X->R differentiable on int X, closed, strictly convex
V subseteq X nonempty closed convex
x_t in int X for t=1,...,T; x_0 interior from algorithm
T is positive finite horizon, needed for eta_T and max over 0,...,T-1
nodes.indexing_note: Printed monotonicity includes eta_{T+1}, although algorithm declares only eta_1,...,eta_T. Proof uses only t=1,...,T-1. Preserve this as INDEX_AMBIGUITY, do not silently rewrite literal source.

nodes.statement: For each t there exists g_t in partial ell_t(x_t) such that <eta_t*g_t+grad psi(x_t)-grad psi(x_{t-1}),u-x_t> >=0 for every u in V.
nodes.quantifier_order: For each t, one g_t works for all u in V; not a separate g_t chosen per competitor.

nodes.statement: eta_t*(ell_t(x_t)-ell_t(u)) <= <eta_t*g_t,x_t-u>.
hypotheses: u,x_t in V subseteq dom ell_t

nodes.statement: eta_t*(ell_t(x_t)-ell_t(u)) <= <grad psi(x_{t-1})-grad psi(x_t),x_t-u>.

nodes.region: Last equality of final display, citation continues printed266
nodes.statement: eta_t*(ell_t(x_t)-ell_t(u)) <= B_psi(u;x_{t-1})-B_psi(u;x_t)-B_psi(x_t;x_{t-1}).
nodes.substitution: Lemma 6.7: x=x_t, y=x_{t-1}, z=u, then negate the identity; gradient pairing reverses z-x to x_t-u.

nodes.statement: R_T(u) <= sum_{t=1}^T [B_psi(u;x_{t-1})/eta_t-B_psi(u;x_t)/eta_t] - sum_{t=1}^T B_psi(x_t;x_{t-1})/eta_t.
nodes.definition: R_T(u)=sum_{t=1}^T(ell_t(x_t)-ell_t(u)); all summands are finite real values.

nodes.statement: R_T(u) <= B_psi(u;x_0)/eta_1-B_psi(u;x_T)/eta_T+sum_{t=1}^{T-1}(1/eta_{t+1}-1/eta_t)*B_psi(u;x_t)-sum_{t=1}^T B_psi(x_t;x_{t-1})/eta_t.
nodes.boundary: Retain negative terminal B_psi(u;x_T)/eta_T here. Both losses and Bregman values are finite; no infinity-infinity subtraction.

nodes.region: Third display line and definition of D^2
nodes.statement: Set D^2=max_{0<=t<=T-1}B_psi(u;x_t). Bound initial/intermediate Bregman terms by D^2, use 1/eta_{t+1}-1/eta_t>=0, and discard -B_psi(u;x_T)/eta_T<=0.
nodes.note: D^2 is a finite maximum depending on this u and trajectory, not a global domain diameter and not an assumed uniform bound.

nodes.statement: R_T(u) <= max_{0<=t<=T-1} B_psi(u;x_t)/eta_T - sum_{t=1}^T B_psi(x_t;x_{t-1})/eta_t.
If eta_t=eta for all t=1,...,T, R_T(u) <= B_psi(u;x_0)/eta - (1/eta)*sum_{t=1}^T B_psi(x_t;x_{t-1}).
hypotheses: same trajectory, loss, domain, and regularizer hypotheses
constant rate eliminates reciprocal differences without requiring a global Bregman bound

nodes.statement: The second statement is left as an exercise.
nodes.candidate_bridge: Set every eta_t=eta in TELESCOPE and discard only the nonpositive terminal divergence. This is the identified missing exercise proof, not a source-displayed derivation.

nodes.statement: Prescient OMD regret contains the negative terms required by the optimistic algorithms.
nodes.sign_detail: Each -B_psi(x_t;x_{t-1})/eta_t<=0, while the initial comparator term remains. Source does not identify this with -eta_t*||g_t||^2/2 for arbitrary constrained mirror descent.

nodes.statement: Given convex V, real-valued convex f on V, p in V minimizing f+h on V, and h Frechet differentiable at p with derivative L, show for every u in V: f(p)-f(u) <= L(u-p). Ambient space real normed, no completeness asserted. This is a proposed derived interface, not a claim to represent all of Theorem15.30.
hypotheses: real normed ambient space E, no completeness assumed
h Frechet differentiable at p with continuous linear derivative L:E->R
nodes.classification: Not literal Theorem 2.8, Theorem 15.30, or the full Chapter 2 observation.
nodes.candidate_method: Convex segment q_s=p+s(u-p), 0<s<=1. Minimality and convexity imply f(p)-f(u)<=(h(q_s)-h(p))/s. Passing s down to 0 gives L(u-p). This source-extractor identifies a possible bridge only; its proof and generalization require separate review.

source_gaps.description: Differentiable Theorem 2.8 does not directly justify the asserted uniform subgradient optimality certificate for merely subdifferentiable losses. Extraction does not declare the assertion false; it declares the cited implication unsupported without another argument.
Constant-rate proof expressly omitted. Its candidate telescope specialization is identified but is not printed source proof.

contract_issues.description: Theorem prints eta_{t+1}<=eta_t for t=1,...,T but algorithm supplies only eta_1,...,eta_T. Proof needs t<=T-1.
Do not infer minimizer existence from nonempty closed convex V and strict convexity. Algorithm chooses minimizers; theorem additionally assumes interior iterates.

A proof of DERIVED_TARGET alone is neither full Theorem15.30 nor Chapter2 observation acceptance. Summation, max bound, constant case, source-specific domain adapters and sign interpretation remain distinct consumers.
